rounds.text: Apollo Sindoori Hotels currently trades at a significant valuation premium, with a P/E of 36.47x compared to the sector benchmark of 23.6x [E6]. This optimism is disconnected from the company’s fundamental performance, as evidenced by a discounted cash flow analysis that suggests an intrinsic value of only Rs 522 per share, implying a margin of safety of -120.6% [E45, E46]. Furthermore, the stock is struggling technically, trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E50]. While the company has shown sales growth, this has failed to translate into bottom-line stability, with compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months falling to -5% [E21]. The business is also consuming capital rather than generating it, as free cash flow was negative Rs 4 Cr in March 2026 [E36], while borrowings increased to Rs 91 Cr [E39]. Conceded: the company maintains a strong cash conversion ratio of 4.00x [E34] and has achieved compounded sales growth of 30% over the last five years [E15].

Apollo Sindoori Hotels currently trades at a significant valuation premium, with a P/E of 36.47x compared to a sector benchmark of 23.6x [E6]. This optimism is unsupported by the company's financial performance, as evidenced by a negative 5% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E21] and a net profit decline of 55% year-over-year [E66]. The stock is currently trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, reflecting a lack of technical momentum [E50, E69]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow analysis suggests the stock is substantially overvalued, with an intrinsic value of Rs 522 per share against a market price of Rs 1,152, implying a margin of safety of -120.6% [E45, E46]. While the company maintains moderate leverage, borrowings have increased to Rs 91 Cr from Rs 81 Cr in the previous year [E39], and free cash flow has turned negative at Rs -4 Cr [E36]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong sales growth [E15, E17, E62] and maintains a cash conversion ratio of 4.00x [E34]. Despite these operational highlights, the rules-based screen assigns the stock a low score of 44 out of 100, signaling a sell-side bias due to decelerating earnings and rich valuation [E61, E67, E70].
